title: Fernway: seed round
objective: Seed investors take a second meeting to lead or join a $6M round.

audience.who: Seed-stage investors, generalist and climate/food-tech partners
audience.context: investor pitch, first meeting, 20 minutes, presented
objections: Vertical farms failed on energy costs
Will grocers give up their roofs?

big_idea: A grocery store's roof is profitable farmland, so $6M turns three pilot roofs into a 20-roof business.

beats.message: Fernway grows produce on the roof of the store that sells it.
Supermarket greens travel 1,800 miles, and one in seven is thrown out unsold.
The best farmland in a city is the flat, empty roof above the produce aisle.
We build and run the greenhouse, and the harvest takes the freight lift instead of a truck.
At our pilot stores, greens reach the shelf 38 minutes after harvest.
Revenue grew 6.9× in a year on three pilot roofs.
Each roof earns $124k a year and pays back its build in 26 months.
9,400 suitable roofs make a $3.9B market in the top 50 US metros.
Only rooftop growing reaches the shelf with no truck and no cost to the grocer.
The seed round takes Fernway from 3 roofs to 20 by the end of 2028.
We are raising $6M to put greens on 20 roofs.
